money.note: Individuals gave $416,821; PAC money $562,212; candidate's own money $0. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Democrat representing California's 15th District in the U.S. House since 2023. Earlier he served on the South San Francisco City Council (including a year as mayor) and in the California Assembly from 2012 to 2022, where he was speaker pro tempore. He founded KM2 Communications.

endorsements.text: In 2026 he was endorsed by the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions, the California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters and Equality California.
His 2026 Ballotpedia survey also lists the Sierra Club and Planned Parenthood Action Fund among his endorsers.

cands.gaps: We found no documented position or action by Mullin on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth limits and land protection, gun laws, policing, or school choice. A campaign-site link says he questioned data centers' effect on residential power bills, but the article itself wasn't available, so we left it out. We found no controversies, foreign-government ties, or details of his state legislative votes in the pages we had.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.name: Charles Hoelter
cands.bio: Retired UPS supervisor with more than 25 years at the company. Graduated from San Francisco State University in 1989. Lived in San Francisco for 27 years, then in San Mateo County for 36 more. Republican candidate for U.S. House in California's 15th District in 2026. No elected office held.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by the San Mateo County Republican Party (SMGOP), per his Ballotpedia survey response. Ballotpedia also lists several online voter-guide recommendations, including San Francisco Young Republicans.
His campaign announced the SMGOP endorsement on February 13, 2026.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Hoelter was born or raised, or when he first came to California. Which Lincoln High School he attended is not stated. No source documents any stance or action of his on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of land and homes, growth and land conservation, H-1B visas, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site lists broad priorities (secure borders, lower taxes, protecting the Constitution, energy independence, veterans) without specific proposals. He has held no public office, so there is no governing record to review. No news coverage or controversies about him turned up in the pages we had.
